definition: An abstract, typically lower-dimensional space in which a model represents compressed, learned features of its input data.
details: Latent space representations capture underlying structure and relationships in data that may not be obvious in the raw input, and are central to how generative models like VAEs and diffusion models produce novel outputs.

explainer.lead: Latent space is an abstract, typically lower-dimensional space in which a model represents compressed, learned features of its input data. It matters because it captures structure and relationships not obvious in the raw input.

tiers.eli5: It is like a map of a city that keeps only what matters, so everything close on the map is alike in real life. The map is small, but the important relationships are still there.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers rely on latent representations in generative models such as VAEs and diffusion models to produce novel outputs. The compression is the point, so the representation is not the raw data.
tiers.paperLevel: An abstract, typically lower-dimensional space in which a model represents compressed, learned features of its input data; such representations capture underlying structure and relationships that may not be obvious in the raw input.

explainer.example: A diffusion model is trained in latent space and its outputs are produced from those compressed representations.
